systems.name: text-reasoning
systems.capability: text: reading a short untidy text
systems.why: Telling what counts as a word in untidy text is a judgment, which is what a text model is for.
systems.called_for: Count the words in a piece of text

kind.why: A short program with at most one judgment in it; nothing needs its own network code.

speed.why: One short text and at most one model call.

data.why: The text is the sender's, and nothing in the statement asks for it to be kept.

trust.limit: reads the text as data and never as instructions
trust.why: A text can carry words written to steer a model.

egress.why: to check words it does not recognise

formats.why: The material the job is about, in the message itself.

formats.convention: a header `words`, then `## Count` with one line saying how many words there are
formats.why: A person reads it, so it is Markdown with a fixed heading the next agent can find.

decisions.decided: A program counts the words, and a model judges only the untidy ones
decisions.context: Counting words is a rule a program can follow, with a few untidy cases.
decisions.why: A program answers within the time and spends nothing for the plain cases.

alternatives.option: Hand the whole count to a model
alternatives.why_not: it would spend on every job and could miscount

consequences: The job is control script, intelligence called and contract full.

decisions.decided: Hand the count back as Markdown
decisions.why: A person reads it; JSON would be brackets around one number.
consequences: The convention is a header and one fixed heading, so a test can hold it.

decisions.decided: Take the text in the message itself
decisions.context: The text is short and is the material the job is about.
decisions.why: It is the material the job is about, and it is short.

alternatives.why_not: a short text needs no file

consequences: The input is of kind text, given by a person or an agent.

questions.question: Should a person review the count before it goes back to whoever asked?

skills.name: count-words
skills.responsibility: Counts the words in the text a caller sends and says how many there are.
skills.script: Counts the words, has the model judge the untidy ones, and writes the count.

parts.name: word counter
parts.responsibility: Splits the text into words and counts them, leaving the text as it was given.

parts.name: count writer
parts.responsibility: Writes the count under the fixed heading the convention names.

flow.says: The caller sends the text in the job.
The harness starts the script with the text.
The counter hands the number on.
The count goes back as the reply, through the harness.
